program: Hospital, school and community violence prevention

acceptance.evidence: givebetter-nyc-final-four-independent-acceptance.json: original-return checks and independent numerical reconstruction; accepted only as explicit conditional alpha hypotheses, not measured causal estimates.

what: KAVI supports young people affected by violence in Brooklyn hospitals, schools and communities.
Its hospital team helps patients and families recover, de-escalate conflict and connect with continuing support.
A conditional reinjury model estimates $127.5 million per 10 local QALYs using the whole recipient's expense.
strengths: Hospital contact can identify people at elevated risk soon after violent injury.
Follow-up and conflict mediation provide a specific pathway to reduced harm.
Original 990 and audited reconciliation establish the full recipient cost and government-funding baseline.
reservations: No KAVI-specific controlled reinjury effect or annual engaged-patient count was located.
External HVIP studies are mixed and suggest sustained engagement is crucial.
An unrestricted gift supports the broader portfolio and may substitute for public or philanthropic funding.

sections.what: Kings Against Violence Initiative Inc., EIN 81-1626947, is a separate nonprofit with school, hospital and community programs in Central Brooklyn. [Scope](https://www.kavibrooklyn.org/) The hospital program works at bedsides and with families, provides conflict de-escalation and trauma recovery, and refers patients to continuing support. It partners with Kings County Hospital and violence-prevention organizations; KAVI does not provide the hospital's emergency surgery. [Hospital pathway](https://www.kavibrooklyn.org/hospital)
sections.monitoring: Measure eligible patients, distinct enrolled patients, sustained engagement, completed services and violent reinjury/mortality using multi-hospital follow-up, including people who disengage. A 2025 St Louis observational evaluation found 7.6% one-year reinjury among participants versus 7.4% among matched controls, with wide uncertainty. [Original study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12379808/) A 2026 Boston target-trial emulation found no benefit for any engagement but favorable, imprecise results among the small sustained-engagement subgroup; residual selection remains possible. Its combined reinjury/perpetration endpoint cannot be transferred directly into injuries averted. [Original study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41587478/)
sections.qualitative: The promising health mechanism is preventing a subsequent violent injury through trusted ongoing contact, mediation and care linkage. Merely counting bedside contacts misses engagement; converting every mediation into a life saved would be wrong. Schools and community healing may add health value, but no separate QALY credit is assigned here. NYC Health lists KAVI, Man Up! and Save Our Streets at Kings County and funds a wider intervention network. That public baseline remains, and overlapping patients/events cannot receive full credit in each charity's report. [City network](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/neighborhood-health/anti-violence.page)
sections.cost: Full annual recognized cost is $4,360,879. Because a measured KAVI patient count was unavailable, the model explicitly assumes 35% of marginal unrestricted expenditure reaches the hospital pathway and $5,000 in allocated cost per supported patient. This implies 305.3 annual patient-equivalents, or 0.07 per $1,000 of recipient spending, not an observed output. Only 25% sustain engagement; a transferred 7.4% one-year reinjury baseline and judged 25% causal reduction are then reduced for alternative help, partner credit and gift response. The resulting 0.3706 donor-attributable events produce 0.341964 local QALYs. Five percent of prevented events are assumed fatal; survival benefit stops after 30 years with 0.85 utility, 1% annual mortality and 3% discount. Nonfatal injury prevention receives 0.15 utility for two years only. Both severity assumptions are unmeasured. No repeated cohort or lifelong crime reduction is added. Because N=C*l/k, changing C alone scales both modeled capacity and cost; inflation is correctly tested by changing k.
sections.funding: FY2024 original Form 990 shows $4,360,879 expense ($3,522,226 program, $647,538 management and $191,115 fundraising) and $4,168,812 revenue. Government grants supply $2,689,257; $108,000 of contributions are noncash and are not added again. Net assets are $1,919,879, including $1,566,596 without donor restrictions. FY2023 expense comparator is $3,389,059. Schedule D reconciles audited expense to the same FY2024 total. [Original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202523219349301002/IRS990) [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202523219349301002/IRS990ScheduleD) A deficit does not establish which next position is unfunded. No current costed expansion plan was found; 0.5 net donation response is a judgment. Hospital resources and public benefits induced by referral are outside recipient costs; this is not full social cost-effectiveness.

model.costScope: Whole recipient annual recognized expense; hospital marginal allocation explicit. Noncash recognized resources retained; external hospital resources excluded.
model.geographicAttribution: 22-county MSA; .95 beneficiary residence judgment for Brooklyn hospital pathway, not a county-measured rate.
model.formula: N=C*l/k; E=N*s*R*e*r*a*b; D=sum(t=1..L)u*exp(-m*t)/(1+d)^t; A=sum(t=1..T)exp(-m*t)/(1+d)^t; Qall=E*(f*D+(1-f)*v*A)/(1+d)-h; Qlocal=g*Qall; price10=10*C/Qlocal if positive.
model.counterfactual: Standard trauma care, publicly funded mediation network and alternative support persist. Only future reinjury reduction credited; no credit for survival from index trauma.
model.attribution: l is marginal hospital allocation; s is sustained engagement; r alternative-help discount; a KAVI-specific share after hospital/partner credit; b net gift-funded capacity. Reinjury and perpetration overlap not added.
model.uncertainty: Very weak conditional mechanism estimate, not measured KAVI efficacy or unrestricted portfolio expected value. Zero and adverse scenarios are substantively plausible. N is inferred from judged allocation and unit cost rather than observed patients. This is a conditional capacity model and does not establish measured whole-organization cost-effectiveness.
model.nativeOutcomes: Supported patient-equivalents -> sustained engagement -> fewer future violent injuries -> fatal/nonfatal finite QALYs.
model.nativeCosts: Judgment: 0.07 supported patient equivalents per$1000 whole-recipient cost, 0.0175 sustained equivalents; no measured output-per-dollar claim.

scenarios.label: Twice cost per supported hospital patient

sensitivity: Model is linear in allocation, engagement, risk, prevention effect and gift response; no empirical precision implied.
Doubling allocated unit cost doubles price; high case jointly changes plausible but unverified parameters.
Public treatment and volunteer opportunity costs are missing; other community health could offset or amplify the priced pathway.
missingInputs: Actual KAVI annual patients, retention and hospital-program allocated costs.
Controlled multi-hospital reinjury and severity outcomes, MSA residence and alternative assistance.
Current unrestricted marginal spending plan and funding substitution.

priceScope: Full KAVI expense / conditional hospital-reinjury QALYs; school/community effects unpriced.
